annotations.text:
The landing page IS the tournament's state.

One page, one primary action, and both change with tournaments.status — setup / signups / draft / live / complete. A visitor never has to work out what phase the season is in; the hero tells them and hands them the one thing worth doing right now.

The three desktop boards are the same page in three states, not three pages.

Every number here is already public.

/api/stream/draft and /api/stream/bracket sit OUTSIDE the auth gate — they're what /watch and /lower read. So a logged-out visitor can see the live clock, the on-the-clock team and the pick feed with no new backend work.

The pool counts come from readiness, which is organizer-only today and would need a public, count-only version.

Phone matters more than usual here.

index.html already notes that Discord is where every one of these links gets posted — so most first visits are a tap from a Discord message on a phone.

Full-length board, not a 844px crop: this is the whole scroll.
